p: Old MacDonald's is pitched at the perfect pace for young families. It's the kind of day where you can wander, stop, feed an animal, have a snack and wander again without anyone getting overwhelmed. The animal encounters are what children tend to remember most, so keep an eye out for any scheduled sessions where little ones can get hands-on. Make sure everyone washes their hands afterwards, especially before the picnic comes out.

South Weald is on the western edge of Brentwood, close to the A12 and the M25, so it's easy to reach from London, Chelmsford and much of Essex. Arriving earlier in the day is a smart move during school holidays and sunny weekends, when everyone has the same idea. Dress for mud as much as sunshine, as a farm is a farm, whatever the season.

For a full day out, Thorndon Country Park, on the southern side of Brentwood, is a lovely spread of ancient woodland, open parkland and ponds, and it's especially pretty in autumn when the trees turn. Mountnessing Windmill, a restored post mill a few miles north-east, is a charming little landmark, and keen walkers can link up countryside paths in the area. Further afield, Hylands Park on the edge of Chelmsford has a grand house and gardens to explore. Back in Brentwood, the high street has plenty of places to stop for a bite, and if you're up for a bigger outing another day, London is just a short train ride away. Wellies, wipes and a spare pair of socks in the car will make the journey home far more pleasant.
